Rashi on Eruvin 6a:10:1.english: There, where there are gidudei - That is, a remnant of the wall is left standing three or four tefachim high from its base, across the entire breach, which makes it inconvenient to pass through.

Rashi on Eruvin 6a:10:2.english: Here - [That is,] I prohibit it where there are no gidudim. Gidud is an expression meaning "lip" (an edge or projecting ridge).

Rashi on Eruvin 6a:11:1.hebrew: רה"ר - משמע רחב שש עשרה אמה, ועיר שמצויין בה ששים ריבוא ואין בה חומה, (או) שהיה רה"ר שלה מכוון משער לשער שיהא מפולש דומה לדגלי מדבר:
Rashi on Eruvin 6a:11:1.english: Public domain (reshut harabim) - Means a width of sixteen cubits, and a city with six hundred thousand [inhabitants] that has no wall, (or) one whose main street runs straight from gate to gate and is open through, resembling the banners of the desert:

Rashi on Eruvin 6a:11:2.english: The shape of the opening from here - At its top, one:

Rashi on Eruvin 6a:11:3.english: A side-post and a beam - [Placed] at the end of the city.

Rashi on Eruvin 6a:12:1.hebrew: יתר על כן - לעיל מיניה, איירי בבונה עלייה מבית לבית שבשני צידי רה"ר, וכן גשרים המפולשין לרה"ר, דשרי ר' יהודה לטלטולי תותיה, משום פי תקרה יורד וסותם, בפרק כל גגות העיר, וקאמר בברייתא יתר על כן, אפילו היכא דליכא פי תקרה, הואיל ואיכא שתי מחיצות מעלייתא, מחיצת הבית מכאן, ומחיצת בית השני מכאן, סגי בתקנתא פורתא:
Rashi on Eruvin 6a:12:1.english: Furthermore - Earlier, [the Gemara] is speaking of building a loft from house to house, on both sides of the public domain, and also of bridges that open onto the public domain, where R' Yehuda permits carrying underneath them because of a ceiling opening that slopes down and closes off; [this is] in the chapter 'All the roofs of the city.' The baraita says, 'Furthermore, even where there is no ceiling opening, since there are two proper walls, the wall of one house on this side and the wall of the second house on that side, a minor repair suffices.'

Rashi on Eruvin 6a:1:1.hebrew: מצידו - בכותל ארכו ולא אצל ראשו, אלא שיש ארבעה עומד מן הפתח עד הפרצה:
Rashi on Eruvin 6a:1:1.english: From its side - Along the length of the wall, and not at its head, but [the requirement is that] four [cubits] must stand from the doorway to the breach.

Rashi on Eruvin 6a:1:2.english: From its head - Referring to an alley that was twenty cubits wide, and they blocked off ten cubits of it, [as the mishnah taught:] "If it is wider than ten, it must be reduced," and a breach was made in that same blocking.

Rashi on Eruvin 6a:4:1.hebrew: לא תיפלוג עלאי - לומר דרב מכשר פירצת עשר בצידו, דהא רב איקלע לדמחריא כו':
Rashi on Eruvin 6a:4:1.english: Do not distinguish, Ulla - meaning that Rav renders kosher a breach of ten on its side, since Rav once happened to visit Damhoria, etc.

Rashi on Eruvin 6a:4:2.english: He found a valley - The common people (am ha'aretz) were lax about the mitzvot, and he was stringent with them, making a fence to keep them distant from transgression, like a person who fences in an open (breached) valley to guard it:

Rashi on Eruvin 6a:5:1.english: A crooked alleyway - whose two openings both lead to the public domain, as follows: (*):(*)

Rashi on Eruvin 6a:5:2.english: His ruling is like that of an open-through alley - An alley that is open to the public domain requires a doorway-form on one side, and on the other side either a side-post or a beam, as explained below. This one too requires, for its two openings onto the public domain, a side-post on each side. And at its bend it requires a doorway-form of the 'pilush' type, meaning one that is open through to its neighboring section; in that case it is considered as open to the public domain.

Rashi on Eruvin 6a:5:3.english: Its law is like that of a closed [alley] - There is no need for anything at its bend. Rather, these make a lechi for their doorways and these make a lechi for their doorways, since we require the form of a doorway (tzurat hapetach) only for openings that face each other directly onto the public domain. Alternatively: 'Its law is like a closed one' means the law of a closed alley, and one must make a lechi for its bend, and this is the lechi made in a closed alley. This is what I received from my elderly teacher, of blessed memory.

Rashi on Eruvin 6a:6:1.english: If we say: more than ten - That the width of the opening of its curve is more than ten.

Rashi on Eruvin 6a:6:2.english: In this, would Shmuel say [it is] like a closed [alley]? - And [the Gemara] should instead say [the case is] with a jamb: is a gap of more than ten [cubits] with a jamb effective in a closed alley? And according to the first version, since more than ten [cubits] is considered like one alley, in a case like this Shmuel would not say that it is not breached.

Rashi on Eruvin 6a:7:1.english: But isn't it referring to ten? - Thus it is evident that according to Rav, a breach on the sides is measured at four.

Rashi on Eruvin 6a:9:1.hebrew: מכלל דרב הונא - אפילו בפירצה דלא בקעי רבים, כגון שפרוצה למקום מטונף או למקום מקולקל בפתחים וטיט, ואין דרך רבים מצויים לעבור באותה פירצה, אסר נמי בארבעה:
Rashi on Eruvin 6a:9:1.english: From the implication of Rav Huna - Even in a breach that the masses do not pass through, such as one opening onto a filthy place, or onto a place ruined with doorways and mud, where the public does not commonly pass through that breach, he prohibits [carrying] even within four [cubits].

Rashi on Eruvin 6a:9:2.hebrew: מ"ש מדר' אמי ומדרב אסי - דאמרינן לעיל אם יש שם פס ארבעה, מתיר פירצה עד עשר, אלמא פירצת מבוי מצידו בעשר:
Rashi on Eruvin 6a:9:2.english: What is the difference from R. Ami and R. Assi - As stated above, if there is a four-cubit strip there, it permits a breach up to ten [cubits]; thus, a breach in the side of an alley is [permitted] up to ten.

Tosafot on Eruvin 6a:11:1.hebrew: כיצד מערבין דרך רה"ר - פ"ה רה"ר רחב י"ו אמות, ומפולש משני צדדים משער לשער, ומצויין בה ששים רבוא. וכן יש בה"ג, דבעינן דריסת ס' רבוא. וקשה לר"ת, דבשבת בפ' הזורק (שבת ד' צח.) אמר דעגלות הוו תחתיהן וביניהן רה"ר, ותחתיהן לא היו ס' רבוא; ואומר ר"י, דמ"מ דרכן היה לצאת ולבא באותו דרך. ועוד הקשה, דבדגלי מדבר הוו טף ונשים לאין מספר. וכן קשה מערב רב. ויש לומר, דלא גמרי' ממשכן אלא מילתא דכתיבא במספרם:
Tosafot on Eruvin 6a:11:1.english: How does one make an eruv through a reshut ha-rabim? - That is, a reshut ha-rabim that is sixteen cubits wide, open on both sides from gate to gate, and in which six hundred thousand [people] are found. So too the Ba'al ha-Halakhot Gedolot holds that we require the treading of six hundred thousand [people]. And it is difficult for Rabbeinu Tam: in the chapter of Ha-Zorek in Shabbat (Shabbat 98), he says that there were wagons beneath them and between them there was a reshut ha-rabim, but beneath them there were not six hundred thousand [people]. And R. Yitzchak says that nonetheless, their usual route was to go out and come in along that same path. He further raised a difficulty: in the desert encampments there were children and women without number. The same difficulty arises from the erev rav. One may answer that we only derived [the requirement] from the Tabernacle, from a matter written in their count.

Tosafot on Eruvin 6a:11:2.hebrew: ולחי וקורה מכאן - אף על גב דלחי לא מהני ביותר מעשרה, יעשה לחי רחב עד שיתמעט האויר מעשרה:
Tosafot on Eruvin 6a:11:2.english: And a lechi and a beam from here - Although a lechi is not effective for more than ten [cubits], one should make a wide lechi so that the air space is reduced to ten.

Tosafot on Eruvin 6a:12:1.hebrew: יתר על כן אמר ר' יהודה - פירש הקונטרס לעיל מיניה איירי בבונה עלייה כו', דשרי ר' יהודה לטלטל תחתיה משום פי תקרה יורד וסותם, וקאמר בברייתא יתר על כן אמר ר' יהודה, אע"ג דליכא פי תקרה שרי ר' יהודה, הואיל ואיכא ב' מחיצות מעלייתא, והכי משמע בהדיא בתוספתא [במכילתין פ"ז] דאהא קאי יתר על כן:
Tosafot on Eruvin 6a:12:1.english: Furthermore, R. Yehuda said - Rashi explained that earlier it is speaking of one who builds an upper story, etc., where R. Yehuda permits carrying beneath it because of the "mouth of the ceiling" that descends and closes it. And the baraita says: "Furthermore, R. Yehuda said: Even though there is no mouth of the ceiling, R. Yehuda permits [carrying], since there are two proper walls." And this is explicitly stated in the Tosefta [in our tractate, ch. 7], where "furthermore" refers to this.

Tosafot on Eruvin 6a:1:1.hebrew: מצידו בעשר מראשו בארבעה - עשר אין פירושו כארבע' דעשר, כשל מטה, וארבעה כשל מעלה:
Tosafot on Eruvin 6a:1:1.english: "From the side, at ten; from the top, at four" - 'Ten' does not mean like the four [handbreadths] of the lower [measure of] ten, and 'four' [is meant] like the upper [measure]:

Tosafot on Eruvin 6a:3:1.hebrew: דפתחא בקרן זוית לא עבדי אינשי - מיהו אם עשא' כעין פתח במזוזות ומשקוף, הוי שפיר פתח, כדאמר לעיל (עירובין ד' ה.) דפתח ליה בקרן זוית:
Tosafot on Eruvin 6a:3:1.english: People do not make a doorway at the corner of an angle - However, if one made it in the form of a doorway, with mezuzot and a lintel, it is a valid doorway, as stated above (Eruvin 5a) that [the Gemara] made a doorway for him at the corner of an angle.

Tosafot on Eruvin 6a:4:1.hebrew: אחד זה ואחד זה בד' - אם נפרץ בקרן זוית, אבל אם נפרץ מראשו בלא קרן זוית, לא הוי בד', דלא פליג אדרב יהודה, דאמר לקמן (עירובין ד' י:) מבוי שהוא רחב ט"ו אמות, מרחיק ב' אמות ועושה פס ג' אמות, והשתא הוי פירצה ב' אמות; ומצידו דהוי בד' היינו משום דקא ממעט בהילוכא, אבל כשהפירצה בראשו לא ממעט בהילוכא, דלא שבקי פתחא רבה ועיילי בפתחא זוטא:
Tosafot on Eruvin 6a:4:1.english: Both this and that are four [amot] - If it was breached at the corner-angle; but if it was breached at its head without a corner-angle, it is not considered four, since this does not disagree with Rav Yehuda, who says later (Eruvin 10b): an alley that is fifteen amot wide recedes two amot and makes a pas of three amot, and so the breach is now two amot. That the side breach is considered four is because it diminishes the walking-route; but when the breach is at its head, it does not diminish the walking-route, since people do not abandon the large opening and enter through the small one.

Tosafot on Eruvin 6a:5:1.english: Rav says: its law is that of a fully open [alley] - Rashi explains that one must make the shape of a doorway at its bend, since an alley that is open to another [alley] is considered open to the public domain, and for two openings onto the public domain one makes a jamb (lechi) or a beam for each one. And regarding Shmuel's statement as well, who said “its law is that of a closed [alley],” Rashi explained in the name of his elder teacher (rabbo ha-zaken) that the law of a closed alley requires a doorway-shape at its bend, namely a lechi. However, there Rashi gives another explanation of “its law is that of a closed [alley]”: nothing at all is needed at its bend. And the phrasing is forced: since its law is that of a closed alley, why must anything be done at its bend? According to his first explanation, it is understood from what is said below, “If [it has] more than ten [openings], then in this case let Shmuel say ‘its law is that of a closed [alley],’” that it works well for Rav. But if “its law is that of an open [alley]” refers to the openings, meaning that one must make a doorway-shape at one opening and a lechi at the second, and not at the bend, then it is difficult for Rav too: how could a lechi on one side, or even a doorway-shape, help [an alley] with more than ten [openings]? For Rav holds that even when there is a doorway-shape, one must still reduce [the openings]. But if it refers to the bend, as Rashi explained, it works well for Rav: a doorway-shape suffices even with more than ten, since the openings of the alley that open onto the public domain were not more than ten. For a doorway-shape is effective even by Torah law, even for Rav, with more than ten, as we say below (Eruvin 11a) in the context of kilayim. [However, one can refute this: one could also raise the objection against Rav, but the objection is more straightforward according to Shmuel.] And there is further proof from that crooked alley that was in Neharde'a, where they required doors for it. Rashi explains: “crooked, like the letter ח (chet), and it needs two doors for its two bends; for otherwise one door would suffice.” However, Rabbeinu Chananel reads “and they required a door,” and so it is written in most manuscripts. And even if we read “doors,” one may say that it was a fully open [alley] that was bent in the middle, like this (*): And [if it is] open with three openings onto the public domain, in either case one must make doors. And from the matter of an alley made like a nedel (below, Eruvin 8b) it also appears to accord with Rashi's explanation, where it says, “rather, he makes a doorway-shape for all of them,” explained as: toward the large alley; and on the other side he is permitted with a lechi and a beam, which means toward the public domain. This is Rashi's explanation. But if “he makes a doorway-shape for all of them” refers to the public domain, and “on the other side” refers to the opening of the large alley, then the phrase “on the other side” does not fit well. And one should not wonder why a crooked alley should be more stringent than a fully open one, which suffices with a doorway-shape and one lechi, since we require that the doorway-shape be visible to all the residents of the alley.
